name: elf_rebuild
description: Rebuild an analyzer-friendly ELF from an ELF artifact (e.g. memory_elf_dump output): parses PT_DYNAMIC / PT_SCE_DYNLIBDATA (Orbis DT_SCE_* tags), adds section headers (.text/.data/.bss, .got/.got.plt, .init_array, .eh_frame_hdr/.eh_frame, .dynsym/.dynstr/.rela.*), a standard dynamic table, demangled NID symbol names and __imp_ GOT labels. With pid, maps each live GOT value to the exporting module/symbol. Local artifact output only; console access is read-only.

artifact.description: Relative path inside configured artifact directory

module.description: Live module name of this image (default: provenance sidecar module)

runtime_base.description: Explicit runtime address of the image's lowest PT_LOAD

image_base.description: Rebase the static view so the lowest PT_LOAD starts here

restore_relocations.description: Restore relocated slots to pre-relocation values (RELATIVE -> image_base+addend, JUMP_SLOT/GLOB_DAT/64 -> 0)

nid_dictionary.description: Optional NID dictionary artifact (same formats as nid_resolve)

export_artifacts.description: Already-decrypted module ELF artifacts that supply export tables for live modules

artifact.description: Relative path inside configured artifact directory

name: process_dump
description: Whole-process dump in one call: every module via memory_elf_dump plus elf_rebuild (raw segments when no in-memory ELF header), readable heap/stack/anonymous maps (include/exclude/protection filters), and thread registers/FPU/TLS when a debugger session is already attached. Writes a manifest artifact (per-item path, sha256, address range, status/partial-failure reason). Budgeted; failures are recorded, not fatal. Read-only toward the console.

include.description: Map-name substrings to include (case-insensitive; <anon> matches unnamed maps)

protection.description: Required protection bits, e.g. r, rw, rx (read is always required)

module_names.description: Restrict module dumps to these name substrings

rebuild_modules.description: Run elf_rebuild on each module dump (default true)

threads.description: Capture thread state when attached to pid (default true)

max_total_bytes.description: Total byte budget for memory data (default: profile transfer_bytes)

max_region_bytes.description: Skip single regions larger than this

name: process_core_dump
description: Write a FreeBSD-style ELF64 core (ET_CORE, OSABI FreeBSD) of a process: PT_NOTE with NT_PRPSINFO and, when a debugger session is attached to pid, per-thread NT_PRSTATUS/NT_FPREGSET/NT_THRMISC/NT_X86_XSTATE; one PT_LOAD per selected readable map (maps beyond the budget keep memsz only). Without attachment the core is memory-only. Read-only toward the console.

include.description: Map-name substrings to include (<anon> matches unnamed maps)

protection.description: Required protection bits, e.g. r, rw, rx (read is always required)

threads.description: Include thread notes when attached (default true)

max_total_bytes.description: Total byte budget for memory data (default: profile transfer_bytes)

name: memory_snapshot_capture
description: Capture a deduplicated memory snapshot: explicit ranges or maps selected by name/protection filter (default rw maps) are split into 4 KiB pages, hashed with SHA-256 and stored once as content-addressed chunks; unchanged pages cost nothing on later captures. Returns the snapshot id. Non-atomic; read-only toward the console.

include.description: Map-name substrings to include when ranges is omitted

protection.description: Required protection bits, e.g. r, rw, rx (read is always required)

max_total_bytes.description: Total byte budget for memory data (default: profile transfer_bytes)

name: memory_snapshot_list
description: List stored memory snapshots (id, label, pid, time, size, new chunks) oldest first. Local only.

name: memory_snapshot_timeline
description: Compare 2-64 snapshots in the given order: per-step changed/added/removed pages and byte regions, u8/u32/f32/u64 interpretations of small changes, how many transitions each aligned word changed in (N of M), and value series for the most frequently changing words. Local only.
